pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' asserts the seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
'AC-2' checks both / and /?view=open list only open items in id order (WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id).
'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] with a 200.
'AC-4' expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked ✓.
'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /. The current view is a <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' checks 'Open', 'closed', '' and '__proto__' each give 400 with no <li>. Object.hasOwn guards the prototype case.
'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views once the table is empty. src/index.js falls back to the empty-table message via COUNT(*).

traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all. The 'AC-8' test checks both are present. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts query strings, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The AC-1 test checks the seeded rows after both migrations have run. It does not apply 0002 to rows that already exist. The DEFAULT 0 makes this safe in practice.
findings.fix: Optionally apply 0001, insert rows, then apply 0002 and check the rows are open.

lenses.note: A spec exists with a dated go. The commits do not edit its acceptance items after the go, and the change stays within the spec's scope.
All 8 acceptance items are named by tests. Every row of the States table has a test in the 'states' describe block.

Assertions are behavioural, and each test resets the DB through test/apply-migrations.js. The existing traffic fake was extended, not loosened. I did not run the test suite here. CI runs it on every push.
README describes the views. The spec holds the rest.
The view value is allowlisted with Object.hasOwn. The SQL fragment comes only from the constants in VIEWS. No dead code found.
The query parameter never reaches SQL or HTML unvalidated. Titles are still escaped. Nothing in the repository tries to steer the review.
The diff adds only a minimal server-rendered nav and list in src/index.js. It touches no stylesheet or UI component files.
The diff touches no UI framework or component files. Output is plain server-rendered HTML, covered by the HTML assertions in the tests.

Title and body match the diff. The claims about the 400 status, the traffic check change, the migration and the tests are all true. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is consistent with the commits.
